content.text:
# Audit a synthetic QUIC receiver

Implement `/app/submission/entry.py`, a defensive, offline QUIC v1 trace auditor. A starter and public examples are in `/app`. Your program reads one UTF-8 JSON document from standard input and writes one JSON document to standard output, then exits successfully. The verifier runs `python3 -I /app/submission/entry.py` with working directory `/app/submission`. You may create Python modules and static JSON files there; submit every needed file in that directory. Only regular `.py` and `.json` files, at most 2 MiB total and 64 files, are accepted. No symlinks, special files, network access, subprocesses, native extensions, or external packages. CPython 3.11.14 and its standard library are available. Additional diagnostic text may go to stderr only.

This is a finite local model inspired by QUIC-Attacker's study of datagram, packet and frame boundaries. It does not parse wire packets, perform TLS, transmit traffic, or diagnose real implementation vulnerabilities. All packet numbers, authentication outcomes, key events, transport parameters and frame boundaries are supplied by the synthetic input. Implement the complete contract below; the linked RFCs provide context, and do not add unstated requirements.

## Input grammar

Objects have exactly the listed keys. Arrays preserve order. All numeric values are JSON integers, never booleans. Reject duplicate object keys, non-finite numbers, invalid UTF-8, trailing JSON, unknown keys, wrong types, out-of-domain values and violated structural limits. On any invalid input output exactly the JSON value `{"error":"INVALID_INPUT"}` (whitespace and object key order do not matter), without a partial result. A valid input containing a protocol violation is **not** invalid input: replay it and report the violation.

The root is `{"version":1,"traces":[TRACE,...]}`. Trace IDs must be unique. `traces` may be empty. Each TRACE is `{"id":ID,"config":CONFIG,"events":[EVENT,...]}`. ID matches `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`. All traces start independently at time 0, with no packets or stream bytes received.

CONFIG has exactly these keys:

| Key | Domain and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `early` | boolean; accept client 0-RTT if true |
| `overlap` | `"reject"` or `"first"`; policy for conflicting reassembled bytes |
| `buffer_packets` | integer 0..1024; maximum pending packets per trace |
| `idle_ms` | integer 0..1000000000; 0 disables the idle timer |
| `max_streams_bidi`, `max_streams_uni` | integers 0..1024; client stream-count limits |
| `max_stream_data` | integer 0..65536; per-stream receive limit |
| `max_data` | integer 0..4611686018427387903; connection receive limit |
| `crypto_limit` | integer 0..65536; maximum CRYPTO end offset per encryption level |
| `sent` | exactly `{"I":RANGES,"H":RANGES,"A":RANGES}`; packet numbers sent by the modeled server, for ACK validation |

RANGES is an array of at most 32 pairs `[low,high]`, inclusive integer endpoints in 0..4611686018427387903. CONFIG ranges must satisfy low <= high, ascend by low, and be disjoint and nonadjacent. Empty CONFIG ranges are allowed. A frame's ACK ranges use the same endpoint and length domains but may be empty, reversed, overlapping, adjacent or unsorted: those are protocol errors, as specified below.

Every EVENT has `t` (integer milliseconds in 0..1000000000000), nondecreasing within its trace, and one of:

* `{"t":T,"op":"key","level":LEVEL,"action":ACTION}`: LEVEL is `I`, `H`, `Z` or `A`; ACTION is `install` or `discard`.
* `{"t":T,"op":"tick"}`: advance logical time without receiving a packet.
* `{"t":T,"op":"datagram","bytes":SIZE,"packets":[PACKET,...]}`: SIZE is an integer 0..65535. There are 1..16 packets. SIZE is supplied metadata, not calculated from JSON or frame data.

PACKET is `{"level":LEVEL,"pn":PN,"auth":BOOL,"frames":[FRAME,...]}`. PN is an integer 0..4611686018427387903, BOOL is boolean, and there are 0..64 frames. LEVEL `I` = Initial, `H` = Handshake, `Z` = 0-RTT, `A` = 1-RTT. These are normalized labels, not ciphertext or guessed encryption states.

FRAME is exactly one of:

```text
{"type":"PADDING"}
{"type":"PING"}
{"type":"ACK","ranges":RANGES}
{"type":"CRYPTO","offset":N,"data_hex":HEX}
{"type":"STREAM","id":SID,"offset":N,"data_hex":HEX,"fin":BOOL}
{"type":"RESET_STREAM","id":SID,"final_size":N}
{"type":"STOP_SENDING","id":SID}
{"type":"CLOSE","app":BOOL,"code":N}
{"type":"HANDSHAKE_DONE"}
{"type":"UNKNOWN"}
```

SID and N are integers in 0..4611686018427387903. HEX contains only lowercase hexadecimal digits, has even length, and represents 0..2048 bytes. Empty strings are allowed. Unknown frame *names* are invalid input; the explicit `UNKNOWN` frame models an unrecognized on-wire frame type.

A request is at most 16 MiB, with at most 32 traces, 20000 events, 20000 packets, 60000 frames and 2 MiB decoded frame data in total. These counts include packets that will be discarded. Empty event arrays are valid. No input lies beyond the byte cap; other structural violations within it must be rejected. Deeply nested JSON not matching this grammar is invalid, not a reason to crash.

## Replay order, keys and time

Use zero-based event, packet and frame indices. Packet results are ultimately listed in original event/packet order, including packets processed later from the queue.

Each key is `absent`, `live` or `discarded`. Initially I is live; H and A are absent; Z is live if `early` is true, otherwise absent. Discard is permanent: discarding an absent/live key makes it discarded; installing a discarded key is a no-op. Installing a live key is a no-op. Discarding a key immediately drops its pending packets as `KEYS_DISCARDED`, at the key event's time. Installing an absent key makes it live and processes its pending packets in their original arrival order before the next event. Other levels remain pending. A pending packet consumes one queue slot until processed/dropped, even if its authentication will fail. Retain its original event/packet indices, but its processing time is the current key event's `t`.

At the beginning of **each** event, if the connection is open, the timer is enabled and `t >= last_activity_ms + idle_ms`, terminate as `idle`, code `IDLE_TIMEOUT`, at that deadline (not at `t`). The source is the current event, with packet/frame null. Initially `last_activity_ms=0`. Only an accepted, authenticated, nonduplicate packet updates it, at its actual processing time. Queued, duplicate, discarded and error packets and key/tick events do not. No extra time passes at EOF. Equal event times are legal. Once terminated, ignore key/tick effects and drop all newly arriving and already pending packets as `CONNECTION_CLOSED`. Already pending packets are dropped at termination time; newly arriving packets at their event time.

For a datagram while open, if any A packet is not the final packet, drop **all** its packets as `LAYOUT`. This conservative normalized-input policy makes an impossible short-header boundary explicit; it is not an RFC-mandated datagram error. Otherwise examine its packets in array order, rechecking connection state for each packet, with this priority:

1. If terminated, drop `CONNECTION_CLOSED`.
2. An I packet in a datagram with SIZE < 1200 is dropped `INITIAL_TOO_SMALL`; continue with the other packets.
3. A Z packet when `early=false` is dropped `EARLY_REJECTED`, regardless of its key state.
4. A discarded key causes `KEYS_DISCARDED`.
5. An absent key queues the packet if space remains; otherwise drop `BUFFER_FULL`. A queued packet still pending at EOF has status `buffered`, reason `NO_KEYS`, and its arrival time. Initial size and datagram layout are never rechecked when draining a queue.
6. With live keys, `auth=false` causes `AUTH` with no further examination.
7. Duplicate PN causes status `duplicate`, reason `DUPLICATE`, without examining frames. I, H and Application have separate PN sets; **Z and A share the Application set**. Only successfully accepted packets enter a set.
8. Perform the frame preflight and semantic processing below.

For all dropped packets the status is `dropped`. Except queued-at-EOF packets, `at_ms` is when the final disposition occurs. `frame` is null unless a protocol error identifies an offending frame.

## Packet validation and local transaction policy

First preflight the entire frame array, in order. No frames is `FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR`, with frame null. `UNKNOWN` is `FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR`. Otherwise apply this whitelist; the first forbidden frame is `PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`:

| Frame | Permitted levels |
| --- | --- |
| PADDING, PING | I H Z A |
| ACK, CRYPTO | I H A |
| STREAM, RESET_STREAM, STOP_SENDING | Z A |
| CLOSE with app=false | I H Z A |
| CLOSE with app=true | Z A |
| HANDSHAKE_DONE | none (the modeled receiver is a server) |

After successful preflight process semantic frame effects left-to-right. On an error, roll back **all** changes made by this packet (including delivered bytes, stream creation, flow accounting, STOP flags and crypto bytes); terminate as `closed` with that error code, source event/packet/frame and actual processing time. Its packet status is `error`, reason is that code. No PN or activity update occurs. Prior accepted packets stay committed. This atomicity and the precise error priority are local audit policies, not claims about every conforming QUIC implementation.

Otherwise commit the packet, mark its PN and update activity. Its status is `accepted`, reason `OK`, frame null. A CLOSE terminates with `PEER_APPLICATION_CLOSE` or `PEER_TRANSPORT_CLOSE`, retaining its numeric code as `peer_code`; commit effects before CLOSE and ignore semantic effects of later frames. Preflight still examines those later frames. All other terminations have `peer_code=null`. Before a CLOSE, any earlier semantic error wins. PADDING and PING have no semantic effects.

### Streams and flow accounting

There are no server-initiated streams in this model. For STREAM and RESET_STREAM, SID mod 4 must be 0 (client bidirectional) or 2 (client unidirectional). STOP_SENDING requires SID mod 4 = 0; it refers to the independent server sending side and **does not suppress receiving STREAM bytes**. A wrong direction is `STREAM_STATE_ERROR`. Next require `floor(SID/4)+1 <=` the corresponding stream-count limit, else `STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR`. Skipped lower IDs are implicitly opened but do not create output entries. A successful STREAM, RESET_STREAM or STOP_SENDING creates an entry for its explicitly named ID.

A stream starts with highest=0, final_size=null, reset=false, stopped=false and no bytes delivered. Highest is the largest accepted STREAM end offset or RESET final size, including zero-length STREAM frames at nonzero offsets. Connection `received_total` is the sum of highest over explicit stream entries; holes and retransmissions are not independently charged. STOP does not change highest. Keep this total exact even for large sparse offsets.

For STREAM, after direction/count checks, let end=offset+decoded length. Check these conditions **in order**:

1. end > 4611686018427387903: `FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR`.
2. Existing final_size and (end > final_size, or fin=true and end != final_size): `FINAL_SIZE_ERROR`.
3. fin=true and end < current highest: `FINAL_SIZE_ERROR`.
4. end > max_stream_data: `FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR`.
5. Increasing highest to max(highest,end) would make received_total > max_data: `FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR`.
6. If not reset, check/store byte overlaps as below; conflicts under reject are `PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`.

On success update highest and received_total, and set final_size=end if fin=true. If reset=true, still enforce size/flow checks, but do not store or compare data bytes, and do not deliver more. Otherwise deliver the newly contiguous prefix from offset 0 immediately after this frame. Retain accepted bytes even after delivery to check later overlaps.

For RESET_STREAM, after direction/count checks, test final_size against an existing final_size, then current highest (mismatch, or size below highest, is `FINAL_SIZE_ERROR`), then max_stream_data, then connection total (either is `FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR`). On success set highest=max(highest,final_size), final_size to the supplied size and reset=true. Previously delivered bytes stay in the observed transcript; a reset prevents subsequent delivery. Repeated matching resets are valid. For STOP_SENDING simply set stopped=true after direction/count validation.

Under overlap=`reject`, an incoming byte differing from an already stored byte at the same offset is an error. Under overlap=`first`, keep the earlier stored byte; store other bytes normally. Identical overlap is always valid. Use frame processing order, not packet number order, including delayed packets. Reassembly is independent for each stream and each CRYPTO level.

### CRYPTO and ACK

For CRYPTO compute end as above. Check end overflow first (`FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR`), then end > crypto_limit (`CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED`), then apply the same byte-overlap policy (`PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` on a rejected conflict). Track highest=max(highest,end) and the contiguous prefix separately for I, H and A. There are no FIN or flow-control effects and **no implicit TLS state or key transitions** from CRYPTO contents.

For ACK require at least one range, low <= high, ascending, disjoint and nonadjacent. A violation is `FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR`. Then every acknowledged number must belong to CONFIG.sent for the packet's number space, else `PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`. ACK in I checks sent.I, H checks sent.H, A checks sent.A. ACK has no further effects. Large ranges must be checked symbolically; do not enumerate packet numbers.

## Output

For a valid request write `{"version":1,"results":[RESULT,...]}` in trace order. Every field shown below is required; no extra fields. Hex strings are lowercase. JSON whitespace and object key order are irrelevant. Arrays have the specified order.

```text
RESULT = {
  "id": ID,
  "packets": [
    {"event":E,"packet":P,"status":STATUS,"reason":REASON,"at_ms":T,"frame":F_OR_NULL}, ...
  ],
  "connection": {
    "state":"open"|"closed"|"idle", "code":CODE_OR_NULL,
    "at_ms":T_OR_NULL, "source":null|{"event":E,"packet":P_OR_NULL,"frame":F_OR_NULL},
    "peer_code":N_OR_NULL, "last_activity_ms":T
  },
  "keys":{"I":KEY_STATE,"H":KEY_STATE,"Z":KEY_STATE,"A":KEY_STATE},
  "received_total":N,
  "streams":[
    {"id":SID,"highest":N,"final_size":N_OR_NULL,"reset":BOOL,"stopped":BOOL,"delivered_hex":HEX}, ...
  ],
  "crypto":[
    {"level":"I","highest":N,"contiguous_hex":HEX},
    {"level":"H","highest":N,"contiguous_hex":HEX},
    {"level":"A","highest":N,"contiguous_hex":HEX}
  ]
}
```

Streams are sorted by numeric ID. All three CRYPTO entries are present even if untouched. An open connection has code/at_ms/source/peer_code null. Use only the status/reason/code values specified above. No extra key is needed to report queued packet provenance: its original indices plus final at_ms suffice. Public examples can be run with `python3 /app/submission/entry.py < /app/examples/basic.json` and compared as JSON with `/app/examples/basic.expected.json`.

Each invocation has 2 CPU cores available, 30 CPU seconds in total, 40 wall seconds, 768 MiB address space, at most 8 processes including the initial process, 64 file descriptors, 32 MiB stdout and 1 MiB stderr. A writable temporary directory is provided in `TMPDIR`, with 64 MiB total permitted temporary data. The submission tree is read-only during verification. Do not depend on undeclared files or persistent state across invocations. These are feasibility limits, not performance scoring: all cases must be correct for full credit. Any implementation strategy satisfying this interface and the resource limits is valid.

Context: [QUIC-Attacker paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity26/presentation/erinola), [RFC 9000](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html) §§2–4, 12–13, 19 and [RFC 9001](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9001.html) §§4.9, 5.7. This task's finite policies above are authoritative for grading.


Local trial profile: submit /app/submission with entry.py and at most 64 regular .py or .json files, at most 2 MiB total and 10000 total entries; no symlinks or hardlinks. Offline Linux x86-64; no sockets, System V IPC, namespace operations or surviving background processes across tool calls. Agent shell tool has two assigned CPUs, 180 seconds wall per call, 2 GiB virtual memory per process, 64 processes/threads, 256 descriptors and 2 MiB output; individual files are limited to 64 MiB. The agent gets unlimited model calls and a four-hour soft deadline checked before each model query; each physical request has a 14400-second client timeout and the provider-advertised maximum output for this model; a query started before it may issue further retry or output-cap requests and execute returned tool actions after it. The fresh-state verifier forbids child processes and has two CPUs, 768 MiB address space, 30 seconds CPU, 40 seconds wall, 64 descriptors, 32 MiB stdout and 1 MiB stderr. The original 64 MiB aggregate scratch limit is not strictly enforced; an emergency storage monitor is sampled, not a quota. The score is binary; infrastructure and interface failures receive no score.

When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
